questions: If there are ties in absolute differences (e.g., multiple pairs have the same absolute difference), how should the N largest differences be selected? Should we take the first N encountered, all ties up to N, or something else?
If N is greater than the number of rows in the DataFrame, should the function raise an error, use all rows, or proceed with fewer than N differences?
Should the t-test assume equal variances between the two samples? The scipy default for ttest_ind is equal_var=True, but this is not specified.
Are NaN or infinite values allowed in the columns? If present, should they be ignored, raise an error, or propagate?
Should the absolute differences be computed as |col1 - col2|, or is there another definition (e.g., signed difference)?
If the two columns have different lengths (which shouldn't happen in a DataFrame), should the function raise an error or handle it somehow?

Should the t-test be performed on the paired differences (one-sample t-test on differences) or on the two independent samples as shown? The prompt says 't-Test on these differences' which could be ambiguous.
Is the p-value returned as a Python float, or could it be a numpy float? The output spec says float, but scipy returns a numpy float.
